security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, after writing to sspmpswitch to activate/deactivate SPMP entries during a context switch, the kernel omits the required SFENCE.VMA instruction (rs1=x0, rs2=x0), causing subsequent memory accesses to be checked against stale SPMP state rather than the newly written configuration.
security_spec.summary: SPMP context switch via sspmpswitch CSR write is not architecturally ordered with subsequent memory accesses; missing SFENCE.VMA fence allows memory accesses to be checked against the prior task's SPMP configuration, potentially granting the incoming task access to memory regions it should not reach.

findings.finding: SPMP (S-mode Physical Memory Protection) does not exist in this kernel tree. There are no spmpcfg/spmpaddr/sspmpswitch CSR definitions, no SPMP save/restore code, and no SPMP CSR writes anywhere in arch/riscv/. The vulnerability condition — writing to sspmpswitch without a subsequent sfence.vma — cannot be triggered because SPMP is not implemented. The __kvm_riscv_switch_to assembly performs sret-based VM entry (line 206) but has no SPMP awareness, only saving SSTATUS/STVEC/SEPC/SSCRATCH. If SPMP support were added, this path would need SPMP CSR save/reload and sfence.vma after sspmpswitch writes.
findings.snippet:
SAVE_HOST_AND_RESTORE_GUEST_CSRS .Lkvm_switch_return
	/* Save Host and Restore Guest CSR values */
	REG_L	t0, (KVM_ARCH_SSTATUS)(a0)
	csrrw	t0, CSR_SSTATUS, t0
	REG_S	t0, (KVM_ARCH_SSTATUS)(a0)

findings.finding: The CSR-swap path only handles SCOUNTEREN, SENVCFG, and SSTATEEN0. SPMP CSRs are not part of the swap set. This is not a bug — SPMP is not implemented in this kernel — but it represents the structural gap where SPMP CSR save/reload would need to be added.

The VM-entry function performs HSTATUS swap (hstatus.V=1 → sret enters VS-mode) without any SPMP save/reload or neutralization. SPMP is not implemented, so this is not a current bug. The structural gap means that if SPMP were added, host-configured SPMP entries would leak into the guest's physical memory view.
